title: Toilet Flange Replacement: Breaking Cast Iron, Installing a Compression Flange, Wax Ring, and Wiggle Test
summary: This Old House’s instructional video walks through diagnosing a rocking toilet caused by flange height and a broken cast-iron closet flange, then demonstrates removing the old flange and installing a compression flange with a rubber gasket. The procedure includes lowering the new flange to floor level, securing closet bolts, applying a wax ring to seal against sewer gases, and tightening the mounting hardware. After trimming protruding bolts and reconnecting the water supply, a wiggle test confirms there is no wobble, indicating a solid, leak-free installation.

sections.title: Diagnosis: Toilet rocks and flange condition
sections.description: The presenter identifies that the toilet rocks and that shims were used. He explains the culprit is a cast-iron closet flange attached to the floor, positioned to the height of the old floor, causing the flange to sit too high and the toilet to wobble. The flange is also broken, necessitating replacement to ensure a tight seal.

sections.title: Flange removal and height adjustment
sections.description: The plan is to replace the broken flange with a compression-type flange and rubber gasket. The installer marks the tile to determine how far down the flange must go and chisels the floor to drop the flange to the proper level, ensuring a solid seating against the floor.

sections.title: Flange seating verification
sections.description: The flange is checked for a flush seating against the floor, confirming there will be no wobble once installed.

sections.title: Installing compression flange and gasket
sections.description: A compression flange is installed with a rubber gasket, followed by a brass ring to allow four stainless steel bolts to secure the flange. The bolts are tapped in to seat the gasket evenly.

sections.title: Bolting the flange to the bend
sections.description: Bolts are tightened to create a tight seal between the flange and the closet bend, with the flange seated firmly to the floor.

sections.title: Wax ring, closet bolts, and mounting hardware
sections.description: The wax ring is placed to seal the connection between the flange and toilet. Closet bolts with oval bases and a keyway are aligned with the bolt holes, and the proper order of base, washer, and nut is prepared for securing the toilet.

sections.title: Trimming brass bolts for cap installation
sections.description: The brass mounting bolts are left long for cap installation, then trimmed with a mini hacksaw so caps will fit properly.

sections.title: Water supply connection and wiggle test
sections.description: The water supply is connected, the tank lid is placed, and a wiggle test confirms the toilet is solid with no wobble.
